Commentary.Commentary: That's it from this contest. Zimbabwe fought hard and gave Australia a run for their money, but the visiting side pulled together and found a way to get across the line. So, all that's left is the final, which will take place on Sunday, 8th July, at 1000 local (0800 GMT). Australia and Pakistan will battle it out to decide who will be the winner of this tournament. Join in for all the action. Till then, you folks could see what's going to be in all likelihood, the last session/day of the ongoing Windies-Bangladesh Test match. And later on, the bigger blockbuster between England and India will take place. Enjoy and see you next time!

Aaron Finch, the winning skipper, states that Zimbabwe bowled well towards the end, before iterating that they did make heavy weather of the chase. Says it is important to spend some time in the middle in a match situation, than just practice. Lauds the efforts on the field by his team, although they dropped a catch early on. Ends saying that some polishing is required in each of the facets of the game for them and they'll be good to go in the final.

Andrew Tye is the Man of the Match for his three-fer. The pacer says that he was always working on picking up wickets and hence, feels good that it has paid off. Is happy to have another win under their belt, before wishfully stating that they would love to have another on Sunday. Reckons that his method is to look at the areas and the ways the batters hit and strategize and bowl accordingly. Ends saying that although they have had their own share of troubles, hopefully they're saving their best for the last.

The losing captain, Hamilton Masakadza, says that the wicket played slower than they expected. Credits that 68-run stand between Solomon Mire and Peter Moor for putting up a decent score. States that Mire did well for them in this series which is a positive. Reckons that they are ready for the upcoming ODI series against Pakistan and is hoping to get something in the 'W' column.

There was an unexpected twist, however, in the tale. Maxwell departed and then Head followed towards the end after Maddinson. It went right down to the wire, with the game going into the last over. Tiripano almost pulled it off, but some calm magic from Stoinis saw Australia over the line. Three wickets for Muzarabani and one apiece for Wellington and Tiripano, but it just wasn't enough. Earlier in the day, the hosts got to a decent total courtesy a Mire fifty. Tye was the star for Australia as he took 3 wickets again (he has a 3-fer in all games this series). The presentation is coming up shortly...

A nail-biting affair won by Australia eventually. Credit to Zimbabwe though, it took a lot to take this game so close and was no easy feat. The chase began with the Kangaroos losing Finch and Carey early. But the Maxwell-Head century stand shored things up. They initially struggled, but then the Big Show began a counter-attack and it seemed like the game was more or less over, with Maxwell scoring a fifty and Head looking solid.

FOUR! And Marcus Stoinis finishes it off in style. Full toss on the stumps, Stoinis loves this as he slogs it over mid-wicket. One bounce across the rope and that's the end of the game. AUSTRALIA WIN BY 5 WICKETS!

Not out! Agar is safe! Good effort though from the Zimbabwe skipper. Agar slaps this fullish ball to mid off and takes off. Hamilton fumbles on the first attempt, which allows Ashton enough time to get in. He then scores a direct hit at the bowler's end and it's taken upstairs, but the replays show that the southpaw is well in. That fumble was more than enough for him.
Direct hit! A run out appeal against Ashton Agar is referred upstairs.
Just the one. 3 off 3 now. Slower bouncer in line of the stumps, Stoinis pulls it along the ground to deep mid-wicket for a single.
Low full toss just outside off, Agar gets an inside edge onto his pads as he looks to hit it away. Quick run stolen as the ball rolls away on the off side.
Another wide? Surely no! No, it isn't. The umpire keeps his arms to himself this time. Similar delivery from Tiripano, Agar plays and misses.
Wide! The umpire signals wide but Tiripano will feel hard done by that. It went just inside the tramline. Fuller outside off, Agar plays and misses.
Wide! False start from Donald. Down the leg side, wide signalled by the umpire.
Back of a length going across, Agar dabs it to point and keeps strike. 7 off 6 now.

Poor from Waller. Could have just cost his side the game here. Should have kept it tight. Agar pushes this to extra cover and Stoinis takes off. Seeing this, Waller has a needless shy at the bowler's end and misses. Nobody's backing up, so the batsmen take two runs.

Good effort from Wellington in the deep. Stoinis should consider himself a lucky man. Dropped? Techinically, yes. But we're not going to call it that. Superb effort. Stoinis lofts it high in the air down the ground. Wellington comes across to his left from long on, settles under it, catches it but is going over the rope. He though, in time, parries it back in to save five runs for his side.
An edge now! All happening here now. Length ball around off, Stoinis gets an edge through the vacant slip cordon for a couple.
Ashton Agar in next.

OUT! The set batsman is out of here! Travis Head is dismissed two shy of a fifty and Zimbabwe celebrate. An implosion on the cards? Head just needed to keep his calm, instead he goes for the lofted shot down the ground. The slower one from Blessing, which forces the batsman early into the shot. Chips it to Wellington at long on who gobbles it up.
Angling in on a good length, Stoinis closes the face and nudges it through the vacant square leg region for one.
Slower bumper, pulled to deep mid-wicket for a single. 14 needed in 12.

Good running between the wickets. Stoinis pushes this towards mid on and he quickly calls for the second seeing the fielder from the deep slow in getting to it. Both batsmen take off and make it in time too.
Length delivery on middle and leg, clipped towards square leg for a quick run.
Marcus Stoinis makes his way out to bat.

OUT! Zimbabwe have another wicket! Could this be a turning point in the game? Remains to be seen. But this is good bowling from Tiripano. Back of a length, Maddinson looks to loft it over the leg side but is undone by the lack of pace. Chips it towards square leg where Muzarabani moves to his right and takes it after settling under it.
Knocks this fuller length ball just wide of mid off for a run.

Slower ball on a back of a length, Maddinson looks to heave it across the line but is hit on the body. It falls on the off side as the batsmen take off. Tiripano rushes to the ball himself, turns and has a shy at his end, but ends up hitting Nic instead.
Donald Tiripano brought back on.
Shaping away on a back of a length, run down to third man for one run. Australia need 20 to win off 18 deliveries.
Just ahead of a length, on middle, Maddinson leans across to get behind the line and pushes it to mid on.
Length ball on the hips, worked towards square leg for one more.
Maddinson is off the mark as he works this away on the leg side for a single.
Nic Maddinson walks out to the middle.

OUT! Straight to the man at extra cover! The Big Show departs after playing an important knock. Extremely full on off stump, Maxwell drives this on the up and straight to Chigumbura positioned there. He would have liked to finish things off, but he's going to have to settle for this and watch his teammates hopefully finish the job.
Back of a length delivery, Head swings across the line and gets an inside edge past the leg stump behind for a single.
Blessing Muzarabani returns.
The batsman rocks onto the back foot and punches the ball.
SIX! Hit with disdain! Like his fifty, he brings up the 100-run stand in some style too. Around off, Maxwell throws the kitchen sink at it and thwacks it over long off this time for half a dozen.
Glenn has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.

SIX! 4th T20I fifty for Glenn Maxwell! What a way to bring it up too. Full and attacking the stumps, Maxwell has this in his sights and dispatches it with ease. Bangs it over long on to send it deep into the stands.
Hangs back deep inside the crease and blocks it out safely.

Catch and stumping chance missed as well! Ryan Murray should have got the job done here. Wellington pushes this quicker through the air around off, Head charges out and nicks it. Murray doesn't collect. Even if he managed to take it on the second attempt it would have been fine, as the stumping chance was there to be had, but the ball goes behind him. Single taken.
Wellington Masakadza will roll his arm over.
Pushed away from the front foot towards mid off.
The wrong 'un, on middle and off, defended to the right of the bowler with a straight blade.
Works it away with the turn to point.
Plays it with an angled bat and guides it to third man. One run added to the total.
Shot and outside off, cut through point from the back foot for a double.
Pulled to deep mid-wicket. A loud 'Push on' from Maxwell as he wanted the second, but Head refused.
WIDE! Maybe the ball slips out of his hands, because Brandon throws this well outside the tramline. The keeper moves to his right and collects it well. Nice take.
Brandon Mavuta called back into the attack.
Slaps this off the back foot a bit square on the off side for a run.
Head uses his feet to get close to the pitch and gets cramped for room. Jams it out towards short fine leg for a single.
Outside off, played to point for no run.
Quicker through the air, landed short, it's pulled away through to deep mid-wicket for a single.
SIX! Another one that's outta here! Tossed right up there on leg, Maxwell throws his front leg out of the way and launches it over the mid-wicket fence for a biggie.
Spinning away from around off, Head crouches a bit and cuts it square through point for a run.
Malcolm Waller is back on.
Works it through mid-wicket for two more and brings the 100 up for Australia. 52 needed off 42 to win.
Spinning away from around off, a gentle defensive push from the batsman on the off side.
Drifting in on middle and leg, worked comfortably through mid-wicket for a brace.
FOUR! That's a fantastic shot. Fast hands from Maxwell. It's quite full, attacking the stumps, he makes room and hammers it over covers. Beats the two men in the deep and finds the fence with ease.
The batsman gets to the pitch of the ball and connects. They pick up a single.
Touch quicker through the air, outside off, Maxwell pushes it away towards point. Single collected.
Wellington Masakadza will bowl now.
Quicker and outside off, patted away to cover-point for one.
Makes use of the feet, comes down the track and wrists it to square leg. One run to the total.
FOUR! Short in length and spinning back in, Head rocks back and murders the pull over mid-wicket for a boundary.
Pulled away on the leg for a quick one.
Fuller in length and slower outside off, Maxwell looks to bang this over the covers but fails to connect.
Looped up and attacking the stumps, turning in, worked in front of square leg for a single.
Touch short on the stumps, punched swiftly off the back foot towards wide mid on.
Closes the face and uses the wrists to work this through mid-wicket for a run.
Punched off the back foot by the batsman. The batsmen have run through for a single.
On the pads, pulled down to fine leg for a double.

SIX! Clean as a whistle from Maxwell! Tossed up, it's in the slot and the Aussie all-rounder has no qualms to put this away. Clears his front leg and smokes it over long on for a maximum. The 50-run stand is up with this as well.
From around the wicket, it's darted around leg, Maxwell looks to flick but misses and is caught on the pads. Appeal for a leg before, but it's rightly turned down.
Malcolm Waller to have a bowl now.
Flatter on the pads, flicked away through square leg for one. 72/2 at the end of 10, the Aussies, needing 80 more for a win.
SIX! Didn't look convincing but sails all the way! Tossed up outside off, Maxwell seems to have mistimed it. The ball goes the distance over covers.
Played to mid-wicket region by the batsman. They pick up a single.

SAFE! Head flicked it through backward square leg and wanted two always. Muzarabani in the deep was slow to get to the ball but fired a quick throw to the keeper, who whipped the bails out and popped the question. At this moment, Head was dragging his bat in. It is taken upstairs. Seems to be very close but the frame in which the bails come off, Head's bat seems to be inside.
Gone? Is Head's time to head back come? There's a run out appeal against him that's taken upstairs. Close.

Dropped short around middle and leg, Head goes back and pulls it just past Masakadza at mid-wicket. The fielder in the deep fumbles before nailing the stumps at the striker's end. Now comes the bad luck part. The ball hits the stumps and goes towards point. Another run is taken on that.
Flatter on the stumps, pulled towards deep mid-wicket for one.
Full and outside off, driven through mid off to retain strike.
Slower one outside off, pushed towards covers for one.
Another brace. This time, Head clips it towards fine leg and hares back.
Now Head walks down the track and flicks it through mid-wicket for a couple.
The Aussie physio is out in the middle to check on Head. The batter seems good to continue without any treatment or a pill.
BANG! That's copped Head flush on the helmet. Head misses the pull off the short ball and gets hit on the helmet. The ball then rolls towards point.
The batsman gets a bottom edge of the bat on that one. One run added to the total.
The googly this time. Head looks to work it to the on side but gets a leading edge towards short third man.
Flatter outside off, Head chop-guides it past short third man for a brace.
Shortish outside off, hit through covers for one. Brings up the 50 for Australia.
Flatter outside off, slapped through cover-point for a quick couple.
Tossed up around off, pushed back towards the bowler off the inner half.
WIDE! This time Head leaves it alone and gets a wide. This was again down the leg side, turning further away. The keeper fails to collect that and a bye results.

Tossed up outside leg, Head is unsure of which way this ball will turn. Plays at it and gets it towards mid-wicket. Wants a run then and is sent back on time by his partner. Would have been a wide had he let that be.
Debutant Brandon Mavuta to bowl his leg breaks now.
Short in length, pulled away to fine leg for three runs less than a boundary.
This one is guided away edgily towards third man for a couple.
EDGY FOUR! On a length outside off, Head has a tentative push at that. The outside edge is taken and then the ball goes to the third man fence.
Length ball going away, slapped away through covers for a couple.
Swish and a miss! The ball was on a length outside off.
Quick run. Maxwell pushes it with soft hands towards mid off and sets off for the run. Makes it in safely, even as there's a direct hit at the bowler's end.

Solomon Mire to roll his arm over. He had a talk in the mid-innings break about bowling as per how the Aussies play. So far his side has done that, now it's his time to walk the talk. Well... err... run the fun?
Hurled on the pads, Maxwell misses the flick. The ball goes off the thigh pads towards fine leg. A leg bye taken. Australia end the Powerplay on 35/2 as opposed to Zimbabwe's 44/3.
Full on the stumps, worked away through mid-wicket for one.
FOUR! Angling across on a length, Head looks to guide it away. The ball goes off the outer half towards third man, beats the dive from Muzarabani and goes past the ropes.

Down the leg side but not a wide. Head shuffles down and across. Tiripano delivers it around leg. Head misses the flick and the ball passes above the stumps. Thus, the wide is not given by the umpire. Hard to see such a bowler-friendly umpire in the sport these days.
This ball is punched from the crease towards covers.
Full and outside off, square driven to the off side straight to the fielder at point.
Fuller outside off, pushed towards point. Again the fielder there has a wild and unnecessary shy at the bowler's end but misses.

Hurled around off, Head looks to defend. The ball takes the inside edge, hits the pads and lies next to the stumps. The Aussies go a for a quick run, even as a fielder has a diving shy at the stumps at the striker's end and misses.
Fuller around middle and leg, flicked away through mid-wicket for one.
WIDE! Sprayed down leg, Maxwell lets it be. Gets a stretch of arms in response from the umpire.
Big Show time! Glenn Maxwell makes his way out to the middle.

OUT! Catching practice for the wicketkeeper. Fuller and angling away, Carey plays a nothing shot. Perhaps he tries to guide it towards third man. All that happens next is that the outside edge is taken and the substitute keeper, Ryan Murray, doesn't miss out taking that. Glee for the hosts, glum for the tourists. 126 off 93 to play with for Zimbabwe.
Hurled on the stumps, worked away through mid-wicket for nothing.
Well done, Musakanda! This is cut fiercely towards backward point where the man dives to his right and stops that.
Full on the pads, flicked away through square leg for a couple.
Travis pushes it defensively from the crease towards backward point.
On a length in line of the stumps, Head stands tall and defends it from the crease with a straight bat.
WIDE! Sprayed straight, this goes down leg. Head lets it be and it is wided.
Hurled outside off, pushed away towards point.
Short in length, heaved away through mid-wicket for one.
FOUR! What a welcome! Full and outside off, Carey gets his stride out and drives it through the gap between mid off and covers.
Donald Tiripano is the first change for Zimbabwe with the ball.

Huge appeal, to no avail! Loopy ball around leg, Carey misses the sweep and gets it off his pads to the on side. The batters cross even as the Zimbabweans appeal. No, says the umpire as the ball pitched outside leg. A leg bye it is.
Tossed up around middle and leg, Carey looks to defend but gets an inside edge onto his pads.
Head turns this one through mid-wicket and gets to the other end.
Short one again, pulled away through mid-wicket for one.
Slower one around middle and leg, defended from the crease.
The man with the name of a body part as his second name walks out next. Yes, Travis Head!

OUT! Wellington Masakadza strikes! Gets rid of the big fish Aaron Finch quickly. The left arm bowler tossed this one up to Finch, who was backing away. The line was around leg, to deny the batter the advantage of room that he was making. As a result, the Aussie skipper goes back and pulls it towards deep mid-wicket. Easy peasy for Tarisai Musakanda, who had to move some steps to his left and take it. Joy for the hosts.

In the air but safe! Fuller and in line of the stumps, Carey looks to go downtown. He gets more height than distance. The ball lands well inside the long on ropes. Tiripano gets there from mid on and saves a couple.
Short in length on the stumps, pulled away through square leg for one.
WIDE! Sprayed down leg, Finch misses the flick.
Hurled on the pads, tucked away to fine leg for one.
Width on offer, but hit straight to point.
On a length around middle and leg, Aaron flicks it through mid-wicket for one.
Length ball on the pads, Carey flicks it away round the corner for one.
Blessing Muzarabani to run in from the other end.
Half-tracker again, pulled away to the on side for one. 8 runs to begin the defense from the hosts.

FOUR! Improvisation. But is it needed so early? Quicker one around off and middle, Carey gets low and scoops it over the keeper. The ball rolls away to the fence. With the field up, Alex could well try to exploit the regions down the ground and in front of the stumps, rather than such cheeky strokes.
Loopy this time in line of the stumps, Carey looks to work it away but gets a soft leading edge down the track.
Flatter again, Finch goes back and turns it through mid-wicket to get off nought.
Dropped on a shorter length around middle and leg, Carey goes back and pulls it to deep mid-wicket for one to get going.
Masakadza begins with a flatter one on the pads. Finch misses the flick. The ball goes off the pads towards fine leg and they run a leg bye..

We are back for the second half. Aaron Finch will open and he has a different partner today. His deputy Alex Carey will stand at the other end. Good move from the Aussies. Wellington Masakadza will take the ball first up. Here we go...
